The '''2003 FA Community Shield''' (also known as '''The FA Community Shield in partnership with [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 81st staging of the [[FA Community Shield]], an annual football match contested by the reigning champions of the [[Premier League]] and the holders of the [[FA Cup]]. It was held at Cardiff's [[Millennium Stadium]] on 10 August 2003. The match pitted [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], champions of the [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2002–03 Premier League]] against Shield holders [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who beat [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 1–0 in the [[2003 FA Cup final]]. Manchester United won the Shield 4–3 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]], as neither side could be separated after a 1–1 draw in 90 minutes.

This was Manchester United's 22nd Community Shield appearance and Arsenal's 17th. Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] assessed before the match that his midfield was stronger than before, despite selling first-team players [[David Beckham]] and [[Juan Sebastián Verón]]. [[Arsène Wenger]] was optimistic of Arsenal's prospects in the upcoming season despite having only made minor changes to his squad, and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s emergence as a competitor following [[Roman Abramovich]]'s takeover. Having been linked with a transfer away in the summer, Arsenal captain [[Patrick Vieira]] revealed before the game his intention to stay at the club.

Goalkeepers [[Tim Howard]] and [[Jens Lehmann]] made their competitive debuts for their respective clubs in the match. [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] started in midfield for Manchester United and [[Paul Scholes]] played behind the main striker, [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]]. For Arsenal, [[Kolo Touré]] partnered [[Sol Campbell]] in central defence as [[Martin Keown]] was absent. [[Mikaël Silvestre]] gave Manchester United the lead in the 15th minute from a corner, but [[Thierry Henry]] equalised for Arsenal five minutes later from a free-kick. In the second half, substitute [[Francis Jeffers]] was sent off for kicking out at [[Phil Neville]]. Neither team was able to score in the remaining time, so the match was decided by a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Howard saved the decisive spot-kick taken by [[Robert Pires]], winning United their first Shield since [[1997 FA Charity Shield|1997]]. On the other hand, this was Arsenal's first defeat since [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]].

Both managers were pleased with their teams' performances, in particular Ferguson, who felt his players coped well in the heat. The 2003 Community Shield brought its lowest crowd since [[1995 FA Charity Shield|1995]]; Wenger reasoned there was "less and less appetite" for the event.

==Background==
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913, it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=The Times  |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the league champions of the top division and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Shield: From the beginning |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |publisher=Manchester City F.C |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 }}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=3 July 2014}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] acted as the host of the Shield from 1974.<ref name="faru">{{cite web|title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609184712/http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |archive-date=9 June 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> Cardiff's [[Millennium Stadium]] was hosting the Shield for the third time; it took over as the venue for the event while [[Wembley Stadium]] underwent a six-year renovation between 2001 and 2006.<ref name="faru"/>

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] qualified for the 2003 FA Community Shield by winning the Premier League – their eighth championship in 11 years.<ref name="ferg">{{Cite news |first=Howard |last=Nurse |title=Ferguson's best yet |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/2984545.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=4 May 2003 |access-date=13 August 2012}}</ref> Despite making their worst start to a league campaign since the [[1989–90 Manchester United F.C. season|1989–90]] season, the team finished five points clear of second-placed [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], the pre-season favourites.<ref name="ferg"/> Arsenal's campaign was compensated by an appearance in the [[2003 FA Cup final]]; the team beat [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 1–0 to retain the trophy and qualify for the Community Shield.<ref>{{Cite news |first=Paul |last=Wilson |title=Pires aim is true for muted Gunners |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/may/18/match.facup |newspaper=The Observer |publisher=Guardian News and Media |location=London |date=18 May 2003 |access-date=23 June 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Bountiful game: Did the football season ever go away? |page=24 |newspaper=The Guardian|publisher=Guardian News and Media |location=London |date=9 August 2003 }}</ref>

Manchester United were appearing in the Community Shield for the 22nd time, having won 10 outright ([[1908 FA Charity Shield|1908]], [[1911 FA Charity Shield|1911]], [[1952 FA Charity Shield|1952]], [[1956 FA Charity Shield|1956]], [[1957 FA Charity Shield|1957]], [[1983 FA Charity Shield|1983]], [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]], [[1994 FA Charity Shield|1994]], [[1996 FA Charity Shield|1996]], [[1997 FA Charity Shield|1997]]), sharing four ([[1965 FA Charity Shield|1965]], [[1967 FA Charity Shield|1967]], [[1977 FA Charity Shield|1977]], [[1990 FA Charity Shield|1990]]) and losing seven ([[1948 FA Charity Shield|1948]], [[1963 FA Charity Shield|1963]], [[1985 FA Charity Shield|1985]], [[1998 FA Charity Shield|1998]], [[1999 FA Charity Shield|1999]], [[2000 FA Charity Shield|2000]], [[2001 FA Charity Shield|2001]]). In contrast, Arsenal appeared in 16 previous Shields, likewise winning 10 outright ([[1930 FA Charity Shield|1930]], [[1931 FA Charity Shield|1931]], [[1933 FA Charity Shield|1933]], [[1934 FA Charity Shield|1934]], [[1938 FA Charity Shield|1938]], 1948, [[1953 FA Charity Shield|1953]], 1998, 1999, [[2002 FA Community Shield|2002]]), while sharing one ([[1991 FA Charity Shield|1991]]) and losing five ([[1935 FA Charity Shield|1935]], [[1936 FA Charity Shield|1936]], [[1979 FA Charity Shield|1979]], [[1989 FA Charity Shield|1989]], 1993). This was the fifth meeting between the two clubs in the Community Shield; Arsenal won three of those meetings to Manchester United's one. Manchester United's victory came in 1993 in the first drawn Charity Shield match since 1974 to be decided by penalty shoot-out.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |title=List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation (RSSSF) |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=11 January 2014 |first=James |last=Ross}}</ref>

==Pre-match==
Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] said before the Community Shield that new signings [[Eric Djemba-Djemba]] and [[José Kléberson|Kléberson]] had made his midfield stronger, in spite of selling first-team players [[David Beckham]] and [[Juan Sebastián Verón]]: "The two of them give us youth in that department and I think it's important to have young legs in there, particularly with the number of games we play."<ref name="ok">{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Kay |title=United's star quality under scrutiny |page=26 |newspaper=The Times |date=9 August 2003 }}</ref>

Arsenal captain [[Patrick Vieira]] revealed his intention to stay at the club, despite interest from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], who had been acquired by Russian billionaire [[Roman Abramovich]] in the summer.<ref name="md">{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Dickinson |title=Vieira prepares to keep faith with Arsenal |page=27 |newspaper=The Times |date=9 August 2003 }}</ref> Manager [[Arsène Wenger]] used his press conference to look ahead to the new season and felt his team's chances were as good, if not better than Chelsea's: "I can understand that we look a little bit poor and out of shape but what is important is what happens on the pitch and you will see that we look good. To write us off just because we haven't spent £100&nbsp;million is a bit easy."<ref name="md"/>

Neither United nor Arsenal made noticeable changes to their squad, but Ferguson believed both teams would remain the ones to beat in the Premier League: "There's only really ourselves and Arsenal who know what it takes to win the Premiership. It's not an easy thing to achieve. You need experience."<ref name="ok"/>

==Match==
===Team selection===
Goalkeeper [[Tim Howard]] started his first competitive match for Manchester United, replacing [[Fabien Barthez]], while [[Quinton Fortune]] was selected at left-back ahead of [[John O'Shea]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Howard the hero for United |url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=89382.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202151532/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=89382.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 February 2014 |work=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=10 August 2003 |access-date=24 January 2014}}</ref><ref name="rep">{{cite news |title=Clockwatch: Man Utd 1–1 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/3139217.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=10 August 2003 |access-date=18 August 2012 }}</ref> They lined up in a [[Formation (association football)#4–4–1–1|4–4–1–1]] formation, with forward [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] positioned on the right wing and [[Paul Scholes]] playing just off the main striker, [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]].<ref name="form">{{cite news |first=Gary |last=Jacob |title=Formations |page=S13 |newspaper=The Times |date=11 August 2003 }}</ref> For Arsenal, [[Jens Lehmann]] made his first competitive appearance.<ref name="form"/> The team lined up in a [[Formation (association football)#4–4–2|4–4–2]] formation.<ref name="form"/> [[Kolo Touré]] was paired with defender [[Sol Campbell]] at centre-back in the absence of [[Martin Keown]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Nick |last=Bradley |title=Howard's way is spot on as Reds lift Shield |page=19 |newspaper=Irish News |location=Dublin |date=11 August 2003 }}</ref>

===Summary===
The stadium observed a minute's silence in memory of [[Ray Harford]] and Manchester United reserve player [[Jimmy Davis (footballer)|Jimmy Davis]], who both died on 9 August 2003.<ref name="rep"/> Arsenal kicked off the match and within the first two minutes [[Phil Neville]] and [[Ashley Cole]] were booked for mistimed tackles.<ref name="repo">{{cite news |title=How it happened |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2003/08/60753.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20081012124828/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2003/08/60753.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 October 2008 |work=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=10 August 2003 |access-date=6 January 2014 }}</ref> The match settled into "a more sedate rhythm" soon after, and in the 13th minute, Scholes' long pass found Solskjær, who was subsequently tackled; the ball ran out for a corner.<ref name="rep"/> It was delivered by [[Ryan Giggs]] and the ball was flicked on by [[Roy Keane]] at the near post – an unmarked [[Mikaël Silvestre]] headed it into the net, which gave United the lead.<ref name="repo"/> It was short-lived, however; in the 18th minute, [[Nicky Butt]] conceded a free-kick for a foul on Vieira.<ref name="repo"/> From "about 33 yards out", Henry shot the ball past United's wall and beat Howard in goal.<ref name="rep"/> Arsenal's equaliser did not hand them the impetus, for United continued to control proceedings.<ref name="repo"/> Silvestre's cross in the 28th minute fashioned a chance for Giggs, though Arsenal's defence prevented him from getting a shot.<ref name="repo"/> Giggs came close to scoring five minutes later; a cross by Butt found the Welshman whose effort hit the post. United finished the half with two half-chances.<ref name="repo"/>

[[Ray Parlour]] and Henry came off in the second half for [[Robert Pires]] and [[Sylvain Wiltord]]. United created an early chance, but Van Nistelrooy was unable to make the most of Giggs' delivery. The player went down in the [[penalty area]] under the challenge of Campbell, prompting United players to appeal for a penalty; however, referee [[Steve Bennett (referee)|Steve Bennett]] decided to let play continue.<ref name="rep"/> Arsenal [[Association football tactics and skills#Quick long-ball counter-attack|countered]] twice thereafter, but their attacks broke down on both counts. Vieira, Scholes and [[Quinton Fortune]] were booked for tackles during a 10-minute spell.<ref name="repo"/> Both clubs made substitutions in the midway point of the second half: for Arsenal, Bergkamp, Gilberto and Ljungberg were replaced by [[Francis Jeffers]], [[Edu (footballer, born 1978)|Edu]] and [[Giovanni van Bronckhorst]], whereas for United, Butt and Fortune came off for [[Eric Djemba-Djemba]] and [[John O'Shea]].<ref name="rep"/> In the 72nd minute, Jeffers was shown a red card for kicking out at Neville.<ref name="rep"/> Ferguson brought on striker [[Diego Forlán]] for Neville six minutes later.<ref name="rep"/> Djemba-Djemba avoided a yellow card for his challenge on Campbell in the 80th minute; Bennett deemed it unintentional.<ref name="repo"/>

The game descended into a scrappy affair in the last few minutes, with few clear cut chances for either side. With no further goals, it was decided by penalties. Scholes, Edu and Ferdinand converted their kicks, before Howard saved Van Bronkhorst's effort. Van Nistelrooy missed his and Wiltord scored to level the tally at 2–2 in the shoot-out. Solskjær, [[Lauren (Cameroonian footballer)|Lauren]] and Forlán scored, but Pires missed – his effort saved by Howard – which won United the Shield, 4–3 on penalties.<ref name="repo"/>

==Post-match==
[[File:Alex Ferguson 02.jpg|thumb|[[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] was delighted with his team's performance.]]
[[Henry Winter]] of ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' opined that, injuries to players aside, "The Community Shield itself experienced most damage".<ref>{{Cite news |first=Henry |last=Winter |title=Scholes keeps United on top |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2409321/Scholes-keeps-United-on-top.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=11 August 2003 |access-date=6 January 2014 }}</ref> Arsenal returned 8,000 of their ticket allocation, while transport problems meant spectators were unable to reach Cardiff in time. A crowd of 59,923 was the Shield's lowest in [[1995 FA Charity Shield|eight years]].<ref>{{cite news |title=United remain ahead of pack |first=Matt |last=Dickinson |page=S15 |newspaper=The Times |date=11 August 2003}}</ref>

Ferguson was delighted in how his team coped with the pitchside temperatures: "You had to be down there to appreciate it. I was told it was 41 degrees on the pitch – I know I was roasting just watching them."<ref name="fedr">{{cite news |title=Fergie happy in the heat |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2003/08/60848.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20080821214837/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2003/08/60848.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 August 2008 |work=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=10 August 2003 |access-date=6 January 2014 }}</ref> When asked about Howard's positioning for Arsenal's equaliser, he replied: "Tim wanted three in the wall and he will learn from that. This isn't America."<ref name="fedr"/> Silvestre denied suggestions that the win gave United a psychological edge over Arsenal: "This is still a pre-season game. We won the Premiership title with a strong run at the end of last season."<ref name="pstm">{{Cite news |title=Wenger sees red over Jeffers |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3139771.stm |work=BBC Sport|date=11 August 2003 |access-date=6 January 2014}}</ref> Howard was unsure whether he would displace Barthez in the first team for a prolonged run – "that's not my decision", though continued "We have four great goalkeepers and we're looking to have a good battle all season long."<ref name="pstm"/>

Wenger was content with his team's performance: "We are at only 80% fitness and still we got a draw with Manchester United," and thought his defence stood firm against United's attack.<ref name="wedg">{{cite news |title=How it happened |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2003/08/60849.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20080907172204/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2003/08/60849.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 September 2008 |work=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |date=10 August 2003 |access-date=6 January 2014 }}</ref> He felt Jeffers' dismissal was "deserved" for overreacting, but added, "He's apologised. He realised he made a mistake. He's intelligent, he's young and he'll learn."<ref name="pstm"/> The performance of Lehmann encouraged the Arsenal manager; he noted that the goalkeeper was "amazed to see the referee wave play on after one aerial challenge."<ref name="wedg"/> Wenger made reference to Arsenal's low crowd turnout and suggested it meant there was "less and less appetite" for the Shield.<ref>{{cite news |title=Less appetite for Shield – Wenger |first=Alistair |last=Grant |page=47 |newspaper=Coventry Evening Telegraph |date=11 August 2003}}</ref>
